title: Given a Scenario, Use Network Monitoring Technologies

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Network monitoring answers whether the network is available, whether it is performing normally, what traffic is moving, what changed, and what happened before a problem appeared.
bullets: SNMP, traps, MIBs, v2c, v3, community strings, and authentication
Log aggregation, syslog collectors, and SIEM
Network discovery, traffic, performance, availability, and configuration monitoring
sections.callout: DISCOVER → COLLECT → COMPARE → ANALYZE → ALERT → RESPOND

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a network problem occurs, choose the monitoring technology that provides the information needed to discover, measure, capture, aggregate, or alert on the problem.
bullets: Stronger authentication and security → SNMP v3

sections.title: SNMP, Traps, and MIBs

entries.title: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP)
paragraphs: SNMP monitors and manages supported switches, routers, APs, servers, and other network devices from a centralized system.
entries.memoryHook: Ask network devices how they are doing.

entries.title: SNMP Traps
paragraphs: A trap is an unsolicited notification an SNMP-enabled device sends to a management system. The manager does not need to wait for periodic polling to learn that an event occurred.

entries.title: Management Information Base (MIB)
paragraphs: A MIB organizes the manageable object information exposed through SNMP.
entries.memoryHook: Catalog of things SNMP can monitor.

sections.callout: Polling asks for information; a trap is initiated by the device. A MIB defines the available information.

sections.title: SNMP v2c and v3

entries.title: SNMP v2c
paragraphs: SNMP v2c commonly uses community strings as shared credentials for access.

entries.title: SNMP v3
paragraphs: SNMP v3 adds stronger security capabilities, including authentication.

sections.callout: Community strings → v2c. Stronger authentication/security → v3.

sections.title: Flow Data and Packet Capture

entries.title: Flow Data
paragraphs: Flow data summarizes traffic conversations: who communicated, traffic direction, volume, and recurring patterns without preserving every packet byte.
entries.memoryHook: Who talked to whom, and how much?

entries.title: Packet Capture
paragraphs: A packet capture records actual packets for detailed protocol and packet-level troubleshooting.

sections.callout: Conversation summary → Flow data. Packet-level detail → Packet capture.

entries.title: Baseline Metrics
paragraphs: A baseline records normal behavior such as bandwidth use, latency, resource consumption, and error rates. Without it, administrators cannot confidently identify unusual values.

entries.title: Anomaly Alerting/Notification
paragraphs: An anomaly is a deviation from an expected baseline or pattern. Monitoring platforms can alert administrators when abnormal behavior appears.
entries.memoryHook: Normal was X; now something is different.

sections.title: Log Aggregation, Syslog, and SIEM

entries.title: Log Aggregation
paragraphs: Log aggregation centralizes logs from many systems so they are easier to search, correlate, troubleshoot, and analyze.

entries.title: Syslog Collector
paragraphs: A syslog collector receives and stores syslog messages from network devices.
entries.memoryHook: Network devices send their logs here.

entries.title: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)
paragraphs: A SIEM collects and analyzes security information from multiple sources and correlates related events rather than merely storing logs.

sections.callout: Receive centralized syslog → Syslog collector. Correlate security events across sources → SIEM.

sections.title: API Integration and Port Mirroring

entries.title: Application Programming Interface (API) Integration
paragraphs: An API lets monitoring software exchange information programmatically with another system.

entries.title: Port Mirroring
paragraphs: Port mirroring makes a switch copy traffic from one or more source interfaces to a destination interface where a monitoring or packet-analysis device can inspect it.
entries.memoryHook: Copy the traffic so I can watch it.

sections.callout: Port mirroring delivers a copy; packet capture records and analyzes the packets.

sections.title: Network Discovery
paragraphs: Network discovery identifies devices and resources on a network.

entries.title: Ad Hoc Discovery
paragraphs: Ad hoc discovery is launched manually when an immediate need appears.

entries.title: Scheduled Discovery
paragraphs: Scheduled discovery runs automatically at predetermined intervals to keep inventory current.

entries.title: Traffic Analysis
paragraphs: Traffic analysis examines utilization, communication patterns, heavy sources, unexpected traffic, and congestion.
entries.memoryHook: What is moving across the network?

entries.title: Performance Monitoring
paragraphs: Performance monitoring measures how well systems and services operate through latency, throughput, utilization, errors, and resource consumption.

entries.title: Availability Monitoring
paragraphs: Availability monitoring determines whether devices and services are reachable and operational.

entries.title: Configuration Monitoring
paragraphs: Configuration monitoring tracks device configurations and detects expected, unexpected, or unauthorized changes.

entries.title: SNMP Polling vs. Trap
paragraphs: Manager requests device information → SNMP polling. Device initiates a notification → Trap.

entries.title: SNMP v2c vs. v3
paragraphs: Community strings → v2c. Authentication and stronger security → v3.

entries.title: MIB vs. Trap
paragraphs: Structured SNMP object definitions → MIB. Event notification → Trap.

entries.title: Flow Data vs. Packet Capture
paragraphs: Conversation summary → Flow data. Actual packet contents → Packet capture.

entries.title: Baseline vs. Anomaly
paragraphs: Expected normal behavior → Baseline. Deviation from normal → Anomaly.

entries.title: Syslog Collector vs. SIEM
paragraphs: Receive centralized syslog → Syslog collector. Correlate security events → SIEM.

entries.title: Packet Capture vs. Port Mirroring
paragraphs: Capture and analyze packets → Packet capture. Copy switch traffic toward the analyzer → Port mirroring.

entries.title: Performance vs. Availability
paragraphs: How well is it running? → Performance. Is it reachable? → Availability.

entries.title: Traffic vs. Configuration Monitoring
paragraphs: What is moving? → Traffic analysis. What changed on the device? → Configuration monitoring.
